utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And Your Honours, with your permission, I would like now to read a brief summary of the 92 ter statements now in evidence. Thank you. Mr. Munkelien was a United Nations military observer in Sector South from 14 August until 1 December 1995. He was assigned to team Podkonje which after operation storm was renamed Team Knin. Part of the responsibilities of the UNMOs following Operation Storm was to report on human rights violations in Sector South. Along with his fellow UNMOs, Mr. Munkelien conducted daily patrols throughout his team's area of responsibility, and reported on his observations of human rights violations committed against the Serb civilians who remained after Operation Storm. The violations witnessed by Mr. Munkelien included the murder of elderly civilians, the extensive burning and looting of many hamlets and villages, and the killing of livestock. On some occasions, Mr. Munkelien witnessed looting and acts of destruction by HV soldiers as well as by civilians. During some of these patrols, Mr. Munkelien and his fellow UNMOs were restricted in their movements by HV soldiers or civilian police who had set up checkpoints on the main roads leading into Knin. Mr. Munkelien participated in a comprehensive survey conducted by all UNMO teams in Sector South of the damage done to civilian houses in over 400 villages during and after Operation Storm. He also took part in assessing the damage caused to civilian houses by shelling in Knin and conducted a crater analysis of 6 impacts from a 128-millimetre multiple-barrel rocket launcher system in a residential area of Knin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll hear from you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, can you tell the Court, to be clear, in judging the distance of 350 metres between the closest impact and the northern barracks as you stated in your first statement, were you measuring to the centre of the northern barracks or to some other point?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We were measuring to the fence of the northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court approximately how far the furthest impact was from the fence of the northern barracks?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: The furthest was 500 metres and then down to 350 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now referring again to P60, your first statement, you assessed in that statement that the weapon, the multiple barrel rocket launcher system should not be used in areas where civilian population can be in danger. Can you please explain the basis for that assessment?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: The accuracy of these rocket system due to the fact when they are fired, the turbulence make it unstable, and the flight also make it not a good weapon to use against specific targets. It's more an area weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. In that statement, you also assess that the time of the impacts to be recent based on visible fragmentation on objects close by such as cars and buildings. Can you describe for the Court what you mean by fragmentation?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That means it's shrapnels, pieces from the rocket that has hit the buildings and the cars in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court what kind of buildings in that area were damaged by shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was houses used by the people in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I apologise, I don't mean to make the court usher stand by the witness. It will be a few questions into it before I ask him to re-mark the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to be asking the witness to take a look at other documents in the meantime. I don't know if this image can be kept and we can make further markings upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It has to be stored. A possibility is that this will receive a number and then later, this one will be on the screen again and then further marking can take place but it cannot be stored under the same number. So if there is a possibility to finish the marking of this document, that would be preferable. If not, we'll find a solution for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, I will simply jump around to different portions of the witness's statement to have him complete the marking on this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can find a technical solution. Please proceed as you intended.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, referring to your second statement, that is P61, if you could refer to paragraph 16 where you reference an instruction to conduct a damage survey. Mr. Registrar, if we could please pull up P63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the present marked document will be stored and perhaps as number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P70 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, do you recognise this document P63?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court what it is?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: This is an order to all teams in Sector South to go out and report back the damage on buildings after Operation Storm, that means not damaged, minor damage, looted with broken windows and doors, and damaged totally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you participate in the damage survey ordered in this document?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, specifically, did you conduct an assessment pursuant to this instruction in Knin on 17 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in at that assessment, what type of damage were you looking for?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We were looking for damage at houses, according to the order given by classification of the damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did the rest of your UNMO team participate on that afternoon as well?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did your team report on its findings from the damage assessment on that date?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the date of the report sitrep was in by any specific timing. I'm not sure if we reported them on the 17th or the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how were those findings reported?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: They were reported either in the daily sitrep or in the special report. I suppose since this one was a special order, it was given in a special report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know to whom it was given?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was given back to the headquarters south and I suppose directly to the senior military observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please refer to your second statement, that's P61 at paragraphs 40 and 41 where you discuss a report by the senior military observer Mr. Steiner Hjertnes entitled provisional assessment of damage caused by HV ops 04 to 06, August, 1995 in Knin. Mr. Registrar, if we could pull up the provisional assessment, that is P64. I apologise, Your Honour, but to Mr. Registrar, to save him a bit of time, I gave the witness some hard copies of his witness statement so that he could refer to the paragraphs in his statements that I'm referring and I will simply ask which documents to be brought up on the screen to save us a bit of time if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no objections, it's all right with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, looking, Mr. Munkelien, at P64, is this the document which you reference in paragraphs 40 and 41 of your second statement?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That's the one that ended up after our report, yes, and that Sector South sent forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the document that you reference in paragraphs 40 and 41 of your second statement?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it the result of the damage assessment conducted by your UNMO team on 17 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like to talk a bit about how that provisional assessment of damage was conducted. At paragraph 41 of your second statement, you indicate that this provisional assessment cannot be regarded as an accurate description as the information was collected in just a few hours on 17 August 1995. Can you please explain to the Court exactly how your team conducted this provisional assessment?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We were given the task and we were normally divided into teams and then we were driving around in the area in Knin and looking at buildings, but according to timing and the necessity to report back, it was a more or less overall survey of the Knin city at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And also at paragraph 41, you indicated that this survey was very much a quick assessment and only a brief view of some of the areas of Knin. Mr. Registrar, at this time, if I could ask to have the aerial photograph pulled up again?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could, Your Honours, ask for the assistance of the court usher once more, I would ask Mr. Munkelien to circle the areas where his UNMO team searched for the shelling damage on those few hours of 17 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is precisely what I was talking about. I mean we're trying to ascertain additional shelling damage researching, and I's ask for those areas that he was going to mark and the only area that I was given any indication of was A.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was my understanding - and I apologise if there was a misunderstanding - that the only area that the defence was interested in locating specifically was where the crater damages were. I think it's pretty clear from the statement that the Court and certainly Defence counsel is going to want to know where exactly team Podkonje searched for the shelling damage on that date. I didn't realise that that was going to be an issue which was going to be disputed, at least having the witness identify that for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the areas -- with all due respect to counsel, the areas where the witness searched for shelling damage, that's not located in his statement where I would be able to track the areas that he looked for. With all due respect to the witness, it's not included in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm fine if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just misunderstanding, that's the only explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the objection is denied. The -- we have now the information but in very general terms, and if we leave it to that, we might miss an opportunity if, at the same time, Mr. Russo would come with new elements which you would need more time to prepare for cross-examination or to further investigate, you may apply for additional time. Yes? Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, if you could please mark the areas where your UNMO team searched for the shelling damage on 17 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: [Marks]. I think that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could have this image saved as well, Your Honour, I will ask to have it brought up after another two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine, but then we need some kind of letter or number given to these markings, otherwise we get confused at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, in that case I would suggest that each of those circles, that the witness place a PA for provisional assessment next to those circles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so, Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This -- temporarily, this new version of the marked map will replace the P70 as it was stored before and this procedure will be repeated, I understand. So this now, then, the map with the four markings on it now replaces P70. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, if we could look back at the provisional assessment of damage that is P64. I would ask you to look specifically at paragraph 2, Mr. Munkelien, of that report where it indicates, and I'll quote, "The damages caused by shelling to civilian establishments is concentrate to the close vicinity of military objectives. Only few (3-5) impacts is observed in other urban areas." Can you recall, Mr. Munkelien, whether as part of your damage assessment on that afternoon of 17 August 1995, you were directed to measure the distance between any of the damage you found to any military target in the area?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember that, apart from the one that we were doing crater analysis on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand. And that, to be clear, is a different assessment than the one we're discussing now; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Objection. I would ask Mr. Russo not to lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is the crater analysis, Mr. Munkelien, different from the damage assessment we were talking about just now?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could again pull up P63.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, I will ask you looking at this document and if you could tell me in your reading of this document if there is anything that directs you to collect information on the proximity of any damage to military targets.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the time that you conducted this provisional assessment of damage on the 17th of August, what did you understand the military targets in Knin to be?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I understand the military targets to be where the UN buildings now were situated, that means southern barracks, northern barracks, and the castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could once again, Your Honour, please have the assistance of the court usher and pull up P70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Munkelien, I will ask you to please circle the locations of what you understood the military targets in Knin to be and to place the initials MT next to those circles.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, at this time I'm finished with the aerial photograph, we can keep it as it is, as Exhibit P70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, may I take it that the MT marking most to the right are the UN facilities, that the MT marking in the middle of the photograph is a reference to the castle, and that the MT marking to the left is northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Registrar, the now newly marked -- oh, suddenly -- can we get P70 on our screen. P70 now marked 7 times replaces the earlier P70 that was marked four times.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we've saved all the markings on the image as P70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, what was the basis for your understanding that those were the military targets in Knin?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It was according to the briefing that I got from the team when I arrived on the mid of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And to be clear, whose military facilities did you understand those to be?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was former RSK garrisons and now occupied by HV soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And prior to conducting the assessment of damage to Knin on 17 August 1995, were you ever told all of the facilities or buildings which were used by the Serb army prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Not that I can memorise now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court when was the first time you saw the provisional assessment of damage report that we've just been looking at?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That report was first shown to me on 10 January this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in your second statement at paragraph 41, it indicates that, later patrols conducted by your UNMO team found more shelling damage than was originally reported on the 17th of August 1995. Can you tell the court whether or not the information concerning that additional shelling damage in Knin was reported to your senior military observer?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: All the things that we discovered that I mention in this point 41 was taken into the daily sitreps and reported to the higher headquarter, that means Sector South headquarter and the senior military observer was aware of it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us whether or not you have ever seen a follow-up report by Mr. Hjertnes indicating that the findings of this provisional assessment were subsequently found to be inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. We've discussed the surveys of shelling damage in Knin. I'd like now to turn your attention to the full damage survey ordered by Mr. Hjertnes on the 17th of August. If we could once again pull up the instruction to conduct the damage survey, that's P63. Mr. Munkelien, you indicated earlier that you participated in the survey which was ordered in this document. Can you please explain to the Court over what period of time did the full survey continue?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Can I have that question again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. How long did this -- did it take to conduct the full survey?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: The full survey means the one that was taken that day, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, I'm asking the wider survey of your entire area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That continued as -- I think as long as we were in Knin, as long as we were doing the patrolling like until I left in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you please explain to the Court exactly how it is that you and your fellow UNMOs went about collecting the information according to this instruction?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Normally in the team's meeting in the afternoon or in the morning, we were divided into different areas and we went around with cars, two UNMOs in each car, and if you lacked car, even more UNMOs in each, and reporting back was during the end of the day, either on the radio to the radio man that was in the team site at all times, or in written statement and that was taken together and given as the team daily sitrep to the higher headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how exactly did you record the damage which you observed?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We put it into the sitrep and I think we covered most of the areas. We were all over the area during the period that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I do understand that the information made its way into the sitrep. What I'm trying to determine is when you are actually out in the patrol, how do you record the damage which you are observing?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We recorded it on to paper in special report scheme, and that was part of the one that was attached to the daily sitrep later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could please pull up the data collection form which has been marked for identification as P65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, let me refer you to paragraph 14 of your second statement where you reference a data collection form used by the UNMOs in conducting the damage surveys. I will ask you to look at Exhibit P65 which is now on your screen and please tell the Court whether P65 is the kind of form that you used and which you reference in paragraph 14 of your second statement.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: As the top says, to the UNMO humanitarian rights section, we were using this form to report in damages, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: To be clear, this exact form you did not use; is that right? Meaning -- I apologise, meaning the markings on these particular form, the entries for the damage and locations are not your own, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: This is not my writing, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would move for the admission of the data collection form, P65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the purpose of establishing that this was the kind of form used or for the accuracy of the content filled in by another person?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, simply to demonstrate that this is the type of form on which the information was collected and not for the accuracy of the information contained within it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Judge, we're talking about a blank form. I mean I certainly don't have an objection generally speaking. I was objecting to the content of this as not being his, as I said initially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So as a matter of fact, what could have been done, Mr. Russo, but it might have created other problems is that to just take out all the entries here, because you are interested in the form as such, nothing else, from what I understand. At least at this moment with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this is clear on the record, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At this point, Judge, I would just as soon, given the fact that it's before the Chamber, just to leave it as is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then this data collection form P65 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, if, Mr. Munkelien, if I could please refer you to paragraph 15 of your second statement in which you reference a report of the UNMO damage surveys. And if I could ask Mr. Registrar, please, to pull up document P66 which has been marked for identification. Looking at P66, Mr. Munkelien, can you tell me if that is the document which you reference in paragraph 15 of your second statement?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court whether or not this is the report which results or resulted from the damage survey which was ordered by Mr. Hjertnes and the information collected used in the kind of form we've just discussed?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, on that basis, I would move for the admission of P66 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is no foundation with regard to this document. This witness didn't prepare this document. He has no idea what the accuracy of this document. It seems to be just a document that he's referring to that he was showed during the course of an interview. The document was done by -- my understanding was composed by Mr. Anttila, not by Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's perhaps verify whether the witness -- Witness, having looked at this document on the cover page, do you recognise the handwriting there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I recognise this as Kari Anttila's signature and he was given the task to make all like you see on the screen now, this is Sector South, all Sector South, so this is for Sibenik. If you going through it then you will see that Knin is also coming up or the area that Knin -- Team Knin was covering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, in response to Mr. Kehoe's objection ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the witness's supplemental statement, that is P61 which is now a matter of evidence before the Court, indicates at paragraphs 9 through 13 the procedure by which UNMOs collected evidence. The witness has already testified to the manner in which the evidence regarding this particular damage survey was collected and reported. The uniformity of the procedure outlined in those paragraphs, the standardisation of it, the fact that observations as indicated in those paragraphs do not get recorded unless two UNMOs from different nationalities confirm the information, I believe, suffices to establish at least the admissibility of the document. It seems to me that Mr. Kehoe's objection goes more to the weight to be accorded any particular entry in the document and not necessarily its admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is being admitted for the accuracy of this particular -- the records compiled here. Your Honour mentioned this this morning. This witness has got no idea of the methods employed by Mr. Anttila to specifically record this information on this document. The proper person to answer those questions is the person who put his designation on the bottom, Mr. Anttila. With all due respect to Mr. Munkelien, he's not the right person to attest to the accuracy of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, you participated in collecting the data which you find reflected or not reflected in this report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the period, we collected the -- this information, and it was my roommate and my -- actually bed mate, at that time, Kari Anttila who put this into report. He was taken out of the team and was working directly in Sector South but we still shared the same room in Team Knin and he told me during the day what he was doing and how he did it by looking at the different reports that came to Sector South headquarter. That means from Team Knin, from Team Sibenik and whatever, and that was put into the report that you see on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Kehoe please speak into the mike somehow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah, just one last point, Judge. I'm not certain if Mr. Anttila is coming or not. He's on the witness list I believe for the week after next. If that is in fact the case, he is the witness to attest to the accuracy of this document, not this witness. If A tells B how they did a particular document, that does not elevate that -- the accuracy of that document simply because I explained to for instance Mr. Misetic how I did it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether every single letter of this document is -- accurately reflects the situation, that's one. Second, if it reflects the reports, the reports not necessarily the situation, is a matter still to be seen but it's not an issue of admissibility, it's a matter of weight to be given to this document, P66 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you, Mr. Munkelien, could please refer again to your second statement, this time to paragraph 23 where you reference an UNMO document entitled "Human rights violations since the start of Operation Storm."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will ask please for Mr. Registrar to pull up the document marked for identification P67. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, looking at P67, can you please tell the Court whether this is the document which you reference in paragraph 23 of your second statement?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I understand from your statement that there are entries on this document which you, in fact, personally observed as indicated on the document itself. With respect to the entries on the document which you did not personally observe, do you know how that information was collected by the other UNMOs and how it was reported?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: You are talking about the thing we see on the screen that happened on the 6th of August, the 7th of August, the 8th of August, the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was done in the same matter as I have testified to where more UNMOs went out, observed, and reported back either on radio or in written when they came back to the team site. Then that was made on the daily sitrep from the team and sent to the higher headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move also for the admission of P67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, P67 was already not objected and admitted into evidence so let's not do it twice. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I apologise, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could refer you now, Mr. Munkelien, to paragraph 31 of your second statement and ask Mr. Registrar to please pull up document which has been marked for identification as P68. Mr. Munkelien, looking at P68, can you please tell us whether or not that is the document to which you reference in paragraph 31 of your second statement?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And again, as to the entries on this document, which you did not personally observe, do you know how that information was collected? I think you've already explained how the information in the last document was collected. Was this collected in the same way?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was collected in the same way, but this is a summary of the humanitarian relation from whole Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And the document itself indicates that it is a summary of the humanitarian violations from the HQ Sector South daily sitreps. Now, not considering the title of the document, are you able to tell simply from looking at the entries, whether or not they are taken from UNMO sitreps?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It's taken from UNMO sitreps, according to how the writing is and, to my knowledge, whatever we reported as our sitrep, I suppose, the Team Korenica did it the same way as we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know who authored this particular document?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Say again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know who authored this particular document? Do you know who created it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was Sector South headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would now move for the admission of P68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge. This is a document that according to the statement of Kari Anttila that he plucked individual provisions from sitreps going from August, when this witness and Mr. Anttila were not even there, they didn't get to the area until the 14th of August, and took them from sitreps and somehow collected them in this particular document. So these are not the sitreps, these are Mr. Anttila's individual items taken from sitreps. Again, and at the risk of repeating myself, Judge, but this particular witness doesn't know how Mr. Anttila did it and what was his thesis behind putting this document together, nor is -- can he attest to the accuracy of the work that was performed by Mr. Anttila. Frankly, Judge, the person to attest to this is Mr. Anttila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is essentially the same objection which was raised to the previous document. It's clear from the witness's 92 ter statement as well as his oral testimony here today that the information collected in these documents was collected according to a uniform and standardised procedure that was "UNMO confirmed" by at least two UNMOs in order to make it into the team sitrep. It seems that this is an objection more to the, if you will, chain of custody of the information collected rather than to the reliability of the information itself, whether Anttila took it out of a sitrep, placed into this document by some cut-and-paste method, I don't believe affects the admissibility of the document but rather goes to a consideration of whether it was altered in the meantime or whether or not it can be truly relied upon, in which case is it an objection merely to the weight to be accorded to the document and not to whether the court should have it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are all these sitreps available from this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have made available, disclosed to the Defence and will present to the Court through another witness all of the sitreps which we have for this period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is there anything in this compilation which does not appear in the sitreps?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: There are some entries which do appear in this compilation which cannot be found in the sitreps which we have which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not have a complete set, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We do not have a complete set and to make the Court very clear based on what this witness has said, based on what is also in his statement, there is two levels of sitreps. The team itself creates their own sitrep as he's indicated. That sitrep is then communicated to the Sector South headquarters. We have the Sector South headquarters sitreps which are taken from all teams, and collected into one document. We do not have all of those but those are the ones we have. We do not have the first level team sitrep which underlies these particular documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Will Mr. Anttila appear to testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Anttila will appear as well as the deputy senior military observer who will also testify regarding the procedure by which this evidence was collected and reported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien has given information about his knowledge as to how this document was prepared and the Chamber does understand from Mr. Russo that there will be an ample opportunity to further test the content of this document through later witnesses. Therefore, P68 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, referring now to paragraphs 45 and 46 of your second statement where you discuss your discovery of the body of Sava Babic. And if we could, Mr. Registrar, please pull up document marked for identification and already admitted, I'm sorry, as P69.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, but the document doesn't seem to correspond to the photographs which we've indicated. It seems to be just the index of the photos. If we could move to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about 06067531 and 32, would that be better?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking now about ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I apologise, I'm sorry I didn't hear Your Honour on that last comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said I'm referring to ERN numbers and not to 65 ter numbers which --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. The photographs which we wish to show to Mr. Munkelien appear at 06067531 to 06067532. Your Honour, if I could have these -- those two pages 751 -- 7531 and 7532 marked separately, actually to replace P69.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently there's a reason to separate them. Then 7531 will be P69 and then 7532, Mr. Registrar, would be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar shares my feeling of why should they be separated? Is there any specific reason why they should be two different exhibit numbers instead of the two under one number?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, I didn't mean to suggest that we should have two separate exhibit numbers for these two pages but rather the Exhibit P69 is actually an index plus an album of a number of photographs which will come in through -- which will be referenced through the statement of another witness. Mr. Munkelien can only provide testimony with respect to these two pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes. Therefore these two pictures should be P69.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whatever you've put under that number at any earlier stage from now on, P69, two photographs with text added to it, same text for the both the photographs ERN numbers 06067531 and same number, last digit, last two digits 32. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, looking at P69 on the screen, can you please tell us whether or not those are the photographs referenced at paragraphs 45 and 46 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do those photographs fairly and accurately represent the condition in which you found Ms. Babic on 4 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Were you on UNMO patrol on that day?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We were on an UNMO patrol in the area of Knin and it was the hamlet of Babici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were your findings on that day reported through the UNMO reporting chain?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was reported in the daily sitrep and reported on the radio when we left. We didn't take the photos. As you see, that was taken the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what is the procedure that UNMOs undertook when discovering a dead body?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Reporting to the headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you conduct any investigation regarding the circumstances of Ms. Babic's death?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for Mr. Munkelien. However, I would like to make sure that Exhibit P70 which I believe at this point has only been marked for identification, I would move that into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P70 with seven separate markings done in three series.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do object to that at this point, Judge, because I would like some additional time to go through those areas that he's talking about. I of course don't object to the first portion where he had the letter A because that of course was what I was told about. But at this juncture, I do object to the balance until I have had time to do some additional analysis on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So still to be seen whether that objection stands for a longer period of time. We'll then delay the decision of admission into evidence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to be clear the Court already made it quite clear that P69 was being replaced with the two photographs. I just want to make sure that that's replaced in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- Mr. Registrar, you can confirm that, take it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I confirm that P69 will only reflect the two photographs 06067531 and 06067532.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe, coming back to our earlier, the military targets as defined by this witness, the TM markings, is that also something that bothers you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, those are the markings that I would want to cross on additionally, not the A mark. He had the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we have three different markings. The first one, the location approximately where the shell impact was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second one was what areas the witness searched for -- well, for damage to be observed. And the third one was the military targets as the witness understood them, that is UN facilities, castle, and northern barracks. Is that something you'd need further to investigate as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The only item of that exhibit that I do not object about is the point A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But is there any dispute about -- apart from whether the witness is right in his perception that these were the three military targets, is there any dispute about where the UN facilities were, where the castle was and where the northern barracks were?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, that's what he marked, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is true, Judge. My objection was allowing that to go in without some additional time to just prepare some questions for this witness on that score.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only for the provisional assessment, the areas where he made the provisional assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's at least clear. Then I take it that you will come back to this to tell us what -- once you have had sufficient time to further explore this matter. Mr. Russo, this concludes your examination in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the order agreed or not agreed by Defence teams. Who is first?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe, Your Honour, that the -- we have agreed that counsel for General Gotovina will proceed first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Munkelien, you will now first be examined by Mr. Kehoe and counsel for Mr. Gotovina or by Mr. Misetic. No. Mr. Kehoe. Oh, yes, yes. You rightly draw my attention to the clock. Before Mr. Kehoe starts, we'll first have a break. We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, are you ready? Then the witness is not here yet. This gives me an opportunity to inform the parties that you will receive further guidance as at what moment to ask numbers to be assigned to exhibits, the procedure for that. We'll change it slightly at the suggestions of Mr. Registrar. You will receive that either today or tomorrow. I'll not change the system at this very moment. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, I just want to ask you some questions about some of your information in your statement, certainly that's not going to be everything but just a few topics. The first topic I'd like to talk to you about is your service in the Norwegian army or armed forces. Now, you came in in the medical area, did you not?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what did you do in the medical area of the Norwegian army?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I was in the medical service support, that means I'm an all arms officer but serving in the medical corps not as a doctor, not as a nurse, but as an administrator or, more general terms, educating soldiers and being officer in the armed forces as any officer in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you spend your entire armed forces career in the medical area of the Norwegian armed forces?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I was in the army medical corps and then I was in the joint medical services, and then apart from that, I was -- and that was my first experience with the UN, that was UNIFIL in 1980 where I was hygiene officer in UNIFIL and stay there for half a year in, as I said, 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So how many years did you spend in the Norwegian armed forces in the medical area?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: More or less from my entered in 1967 until I ended in 2006 I was a medical officer, but as I said with an overall role to administration and 62 months of that was with the UN or NATO assignments abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I think you noted in one of your statements that you came to Zagreb, I believe it was on August the 1st of 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just bring up ID 10-0251 to ID 10-0328.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, under the existing system we ask for a number but that will change tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes D79 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As this was being brought up, Judge, this is a large document. I don't intend to use the entire document, naturally. I leave it in there for contextual purposes, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually if the parties could agree what is needed to contextualise certain elements, it saves a lot of paper and a lot of reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge. If we could turn to ID 10-0258 which is several pages in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in the -- if I may, Mr. Munkelien, this is a peacekeeping training manual for the United Nations military observer course, the curriculum and it is from 1995. At this particular introduction is the background and it notes, and I'll read it slowly: "The United Nations military observers (UNMOs) are military officers assigned to serve within the United Nations on a loan basis by governments of member states at the request of the Secretary-General. "Military engineers and medical personnel may be administered as military observers for administrative and financial purposes." I'm just waiting for the translation to catch up. One second, sir. Now, sir, were you sent to the UN as a United Nations Military Observer as medical personnel?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I was sent as a military observer, as a general officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you were not sent for any administrative or financial purposes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned to us -- or you didn't mention to us. It's set forth in your witness statements that you have experience in both identifying weapons systems as well as crater analysis; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where did you receive that training in the Norwegian army?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We received it in the -- I was in the cadet school in medical corps and then I attended one year of all arms cadet school, that means war college, more or less, it's mentioned war college now. It's one year education.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the first school that you went to is a basic school that has a -- that trains medical personnel and lawyers and people of that level, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It trains the medical personnel, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you mentioned going to the medical -- the military college. Now, that was in 1972, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was obviously, just the simple math, some 23 years prior to your entry into Sector South; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: How many years did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think 95 minus 72 is 23, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you have any other training in the Norwegian Armed Forces in addition to that training, last training in '71 and '72 concerning weapons systems and crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Apart from living up north when I was in Brigade North, we had a medical company, we had artillery battalion, we had an infantry battalion, so we served in the same area, more or less. In addition, I was in, as I said, UNIFIL, and I was in the wrong end of the mortars at that time when Hadat [phoen] forces shelled the hospital in the spring 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So were you tasked at that time to do a crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I never did that but we were definitely looking at the craters that ruined all the barracks in the medical facility of UNIFIL.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you also tasked to -- during that UNIFIL assignment tasked to identify the weapons systems that were shooting in your area?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We were never given that specific task because others was doing that one, but we were definitely looking at the weapons that was firing at us and the Dutch battalion who made an end to the firing with their 120 mortars, we went to them as well as looking at how did they fire and how did they exercise their firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, taking what you've just said, Mr. Munkelien, it would be fair to say that prior to being a United Nations Military Observer in 1995, the last formal training by the Norwegian Armed Forces in this area was in 1972.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, and then the experience I had in 1980. The formal one was the last one in '72, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, did you receive training at the UNMO school prior to going to Sector South, or prior to going to Zagreb, excuse me, in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I was at that UNMO course in 1989 prior to my assignment to UNTSO, United Nations Truce Supervision Organisation in the oldest UN organisation on UNMOs in the Middle East.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So I take it from your answer, Mr. Munkelien, that you did not have any artillery training on weapons systems in the former Yugoslavia prior to going to Zagreb on August the 1st, 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: We had non-specific [Realtime transcript read in error "none specific"] education in Norway, and then we had in brief in Zagreb when we came there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, this might be easily overlooked. If you please, I don't know whether you can see the record, your last answer was recorded as we had "none specific education in Norway" which is not the same as we had "non-specific education in Norway" and I understood your answer to be that you had non-specific education in Norway. That is education that you had and not that you had none specific education.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Non-specific education prior to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But none is now written as n-o-n-e whereas I understood your answer to be n-o-n dash specific.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then this is now corrected for the transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, if at any point you don't understand one of my questions, which I will tell you happens, please stop me and I'll re-ask it. Okay?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With regard to this briefing in Zagreb, if we can just stay with that for one moment. Did that briefing in Zagreb include training on weapons systems in the former Yugoslavia as well as crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't remember any specific education on the crater analysis but I can remember that we were given the briefing what weapons have been used in this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you given a UN pamphlet at the time identifying those weapons systems?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you use that during the period of time that you were in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we will get to that in a bit, but let me just talk to you a little bit and shift gears to your getting to the Sector South area on August the 14th. I do believe from your statement that that is accurate that you got there on August 14th. Now, you noted for us that you were assigned to what was Team Podkonje but then became Team Knin, is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the senior military observer at the time was Colonel Hjertnes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And he had been there for, if you know, approximately how long prior to you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't know, but he was definitely there when I came and he was there when I left in December so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted for the Prosecution, and if I may, if I can just turn my attention to -- when you were preparing the provisional assessment that the -- P63, if I could ask to bring that up. You noted during the questioning by the Prosecution that P63 was the order that was given to you for doing the crater analysis on the 17th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you can read for us the first sentence in that, and this says, "This headquarters requires a survey of all teams and concerning number of houses destroyed or looted, minority people left behind and HR," which human rights, "violations, during HV Operation Storm or earlier." This says nothing about an analysis of the artillery attack during Operation Storm, does it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In fact, sir, Colonel Hjertnes, he was a colonel at the time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Light Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Light colonel, we'll call him light colonel. Mr. Hjertnes is probably easier.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Hjertnes had actually begun an analysis of the shelling before you arrived on August 14th, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I didn't get your question now. That he had ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, sir, that Lieutenant-Colonel Hjertnes had begun an analysis of the shelling of Knin that had taken place during the 4th and the 5th, that he had begun that analysis before you came to Sector South on August 14th, 1995, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I don't know that as a fact, but I suppose he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you do know that lieutenant-colonel Hjertnes has advised the Office of the Prosecutor that the exhibit that we have on the podium, excuse me, on the screen, P63 was separate from the instruction to you on the 17th of August to do an analysis or the analysis that you performed in Knin. You do know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would object to Mr. Kehoe putting to the witness the statement of another witness who has yet to testify in the case and in any case, identifying from whom this information comes, if he wishes to confront him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to verify. Is Mr. Hjertnes still to testify or was he replaced by this witness? That's what my recollection is but I might be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Office of the Prosecutor will not be calling Mr. Hjertnes. Mr. Munkelien was not called to replace the testimony of Mr. Hjertnes he was called as part of the Prosecution's examination in chief on additional matters to which Mr. Hjertnes' testimony certainly overlaps but in any case we've already formally removed Mr. Hjertnes from our witness list and he will not be called in the Prosecution's case in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But now let me then go back to what you just said. "We would object to Mr. Kehoe putting to the witness the statement of another witness who has yet to testify in the case," which it sounds a bit different to me to what you just said, that he is not going to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise if I misspoke or misled the Court by that particular use of the word. We are not certain to what extent the Defence may wish to call Mr. Hjertnes, they certainly indicated during their opening statement that the Court was going to have to wait for the Defence case to see the report of Mr. Hjertnes, which at least to my mind indicates that they intended to call him or we weren't sure whether the Court would choose to call him on their own. In any event, I want to be clear we are not calling him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could it be that by putting questions to this witness you would receive information which is relevant for a decision whether or not to call Mr. Hjertnes at a later stage as a Defence witness if it ever comes to the presentation of a Defence case?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we certainly have no objection to a witness being confronted with the substance of another witness's statement. It is the identification to the witness on the stand of who said the statement with which they are being confronted that I am objecting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't use the name of Mr. Hjertnes, would the context -- the context would not be -- would that not be a bit ridiculous to say -- the person who might have given you this instruction or the person who was in charge there after you've put three or four questions on whether he was there already before the witness -- no, Mr. Russo, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, I don't recall if you recall the question.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That often happens with minutes going by so let me re-ask it, with Your Honour's permission. You do know that Mr. Hjertnes told the Office of the Prosecutor that the exhibit that is on the screen before you --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- the instruction to conduct damage survey was different from the instruction that you received on the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel is kindly asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is different from the instruction that you received to go and examine the crater analysis and the artillery impacts?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. As you see, this is to all teams, that means all teams in Sector South, and we were given the order by our team leader via the SMO, at that time Steinar Hjertnes, for the crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you are aware that he has told the Office of the Prosecutor that the order to do the crater analysis was different than the order that we have on the screen, P63, which is the order for all teams to do an analysis of burnings, lootings, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And of course you would agree with me that Steinar Hjertnes would know better what orders he gave and what he meant by those orders, would he not?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, and I see no discrepance between giving two orders, this one to all the teams and the specific orders to UNMOs in Team Knin, go and do the crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, just by way of background, Mr. Munkelien, you when you got to Knin, had no knowledge what Knin looked like as it concerned RSK soldiers and RSK military positions during 4, 5 August of 1995, did you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So for the sake of argument, if there were mortar positions at a particular locale on either the 4th or the 5th manned by RSK soldiers, you didn't know about it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Likewise, on the 4th or the 5th, if there were troop movements through Knin on the 4th or the 5th, you wouldn't know about those either?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I could ask you a bit about this provisional assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could pull that back on the screen and pardon me for moving slowly, P64, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Munkelien, when you were tasked by Mr. Hjertnes to do this analysis, you were aware, were you not, that this analysis was extremely important, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, like all the tasks that we got.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you were aware -- and if I can point to your statement, if I may, the paragraph -- I'm sorry, do you have your statement before you, the hard copy?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 61 and I'm looking at paragraph 41. And it looks like it's -- one, two -- three or four lines down, five lines down. It starts the sentence, "The survey undertaken," do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It says, "The survey undertaken on that day was very much a quick assessment because I suspect pressure was being applied for some report to be submitted to some higher authority." Who was giving that pressure to Sector South to conduct this assessment?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Like all army, you have always a higher headquarter that you feel are pressing to have information, so I suppose Sector South reported, as you see, directly to Zagreb. So I suppose they -- I got the feeling that they wanted this update as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did Mr. Hjertnes at the time tell you that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: He was very eager to have this information as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this information -- by the way, at that particular time, and this was the 17th of August, 1995, the Chief of Staff in Zagreb at that time was Lieutenant-Colonel Leslie, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't recall his name but if you say so, you have the papers ahead of you so I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, sir, that during this period of time, during your meetings that Mr. Hjertnes and others believed that UN personnel who had been present in Knin during Operation Storm had formed opinions regarding the shelling which Lieutenant-Colonel Hjertnes felt were based on assumptions not supported by facts? Is that an accurate assessment of your understanding as to the position of Lieutenant-Colonel Hjertnes when this assessment was being done?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were never told that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you told by the Office of the Prosecutor that Colonel Hjertnes told that to them as early as January of this year?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, looking at your last question --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm really admiring the witness that he can answer that question, which is: "Isn't it a fact that during this period of time, during your meetings, Mr. Hjertnes and others believed," well, what they believe is always very difficult to find out unless they tell you, "that UN personnel who had been present in Knin during Operation Storm," which did a lot of assumptions ate least that they were present during Operation Storm, all the others apart from Mr. Hjertnes had formed opinions regarding the shelling which that particular person, Hjertnes felt were based on assumption not supported by facts? That's a whole world in one question, not only a whole world, but the world in the minds of others where you have not asked one single question about who told you what and break that down into acceptable piece. But the answer was clear. The answer was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I -- I do believe it was an inaccurate use of the verb. I should not have used "believe," then said "stated" or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have reconsidered the whole of the question, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, your results of your examination on the 17th were verbally reported to Colonel Hjertnes, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: They were verbally reported and written reported as you see it on one of these hard copies that I have ahead of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you saying that one of the exhibits that the Prosecution has shown you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the document that refers to, but I have ahead of me the report on the 17th signed by Kari Anttila and me on the crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The document that you have before you is P60.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can bring that up on the screen. P60 is a document that you have told the Trial Chamber that you signed in December of 1995. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now I'm talking about your -- the results that you gave to Colonel Hjertnes on 17-18 August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That report to Colonel Hjertnes was verbal, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then he took those results and sent them to Zagreb which ended up in the provisional report?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you knew at the time when you were doing this analysis that the information that you were providing to Colonel Hjertnes was going to be transmitted to a higher authority, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I -- it was part of a report so I suppose that he should reported onwards. That was the system at that time and it still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, and on that score, it was -- the information that you gave him was -- it was important to be accurate, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, before we move into the subject of that, I want to just inquire for one moment a few questions about this statement P60 that's on the screen. And tell me who wrote this.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't recall who wrote it. I only know that I signed it together with Kari Anttila.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And -- well, tell us the circumstances under which you signed it.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't recall that either, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, was it given to you typed up as it is here for you to sign?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, it was definitely put together with the best of our knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where were you when you did this?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it was in the 17th of December, I believe you told the Trial Chamber, and that you were no -- you had left Sector South on 1 December 1995; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I left on the 1st of December, 1995, so if I signed this one, I should have been close to Tuzla at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you signed this on December -- 17 December 1995, there was no Sector South, was there?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, it was more or less out by then. I left on 1st of December, and I'm not sure about what happened to the rest, but I suppose by end of 1995, Sector South was out of history like all the other sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sector South closed in November of 1995, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did it not?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, clearly if you look at the heading on this, which you say was signed as of 17 December 1995, and if you look at the logo on top and the United Nations, it says it's an UNMO headquarters Sector South, Knin. That's inaccurate, isn't it? Because there was no Sector South when you signed this.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't see the point of making this one because definitely, it was done in the time when you had the Sector South like you say and state on the 17th of August, we did this crater analysis and at that time, you had Sector South like you had all the other sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, this information, is it based on any notes that you have that -- what you set forth in this document?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It's based on the best of my knowledge. Either I had it written down or it was my memory, I'm not sure, but definitely it was correct what we wrote down on the date, if it was on the 17th of August or if it was in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you're just saying that when you wrote this down, it was correct when you wrote it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It was correct then, and it was correct when we wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's explore that for one moment. If you take a look at this particular document, and you have the grid reference here for these impacts as WJ9778. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That's very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, if I could bring up 1D13-0004. Excuse me, I take that -- if you could bring -- I'm sorry 1D13-0107, I apologise. I apologise, Your Honour, I'm misreading these lists, if you bear with me for one moment as to this. 1D13-0005.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, I set before you a map with the grid reference WJ9778. Now, this is the grid reference that you say was accurate when you did this statement in December of 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that grid reference is not the grid reference that you identified previously today, did you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, actually it's 9678.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Who selected -- who was at this interview with Mr. Anttila and you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Say again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who from the -- any other investigator or anybody else, who was at this interview with you in December of 1995 when you identified grid reference WJ99 -- excuse me, WJ9778?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Sorry, I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, in that grid reference, you do know that the hospital is in that grid reference, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
