utterances.text: So were you shown a map at the time in December of 1995 where you picked out this area in which the map was located?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, the hospital was located?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I can't remember that, but we were very aware of where the hospital were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So I think we testified previously that -- you would agree with me that analysing artillery impacts and crater analysis and direction, its precision is important?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Its very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is at least a mistake on the grid reference?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In fact, it is one grid reference over, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, it's the next square.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in fact that next square that we talk about is significantly closer to the northern barracks, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to P70, if we can. I'm being reminded of my frailties, Your Honour, on that particular map, which is -- which is 1D13-0005. If we could have a D number and a number assigned to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not P70?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, no. The map that I just had before us is a Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I do understand you better, the previous map we saw with the crater reference on it, Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D80 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I'll offer Defence Exhibit D80 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D80 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, looking at P70, sir, the area that you had identified as Exhibit A, that is the area in which you said that the impacts were made?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you noted for us in your direct examination and your statement that the closest impact was 350 metres from the northern gate entrance; right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Northern fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Northern fence?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Northern barrack fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Northern barrack fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could move to our next exhibit on this level. If I may, first is 1D13-0004. And if I could have -- is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you see what we have there is an indication of the fence around the northern barracks and I submit to you that the line out to the red circle is 350 metres. Now, the area that you pointed out in P70 is well within that 350-metre circle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, and as I said, 300 to 500 metres in the populated area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, what you said was that the closest --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: The closest was 350, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the closest was 350. It would be, from the fence of the northern barracks, it would be where the line comes out from the barracks to the red line, and 500 would be yet more north, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the area that you pointed out in P70 was significantly less than 350 metres from the fence of the northern barracks, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, but I mean I was given the map and I marked as to my best knowledge maybe the centre of where the grenades had landed. You had made it more artificial like this one, and I haven't had the time to make it more accurate than I could do on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think we pointed out previously that artillery analysis and crater analysis in those specialties, it's important to be precise, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if you have the artillery taking place well outside the 300 to 500 area, it's not in the location of the houses that you identify for the Prosecution, is it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It's close to the houses and you see shrapnels at the houses and the cars, so maybe you can mark out 500 metres from the fence for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, 500 metres would yet be further north of that area, isn't it? Another 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I could just get a D number for that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes D81 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't mean to be premature, we will be objecting to the admission of this evidence on certain grounds if this Exhibit gets moved for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this map on which the -- is there -- I mean it seems to be an aerial photograph that unless there is any reason to assume that there's any manipulation in that, but apart from that, it just gives a grid reference. Is there anything wrong with the northern barracks fence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we take exception to is the testimony from Mr. Kehoe that the red line indicates a radius of 350 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I asked already yesterday to get a map with a scale on it. This Chamber is not inclined to go on struggling with not knowing distances for the weeks to come. Why do we not get, by the first map of Knin at the nearest book shop in Knin, so that we have a scale where we can orient ourselves? I take it that Mr. Kehoe was so much emphasising precision would not make any mistake here in the red line saying that this is 300 metres but we will check it as soon as we have a map which allows us to verify these kind of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could direct the Court's attention to map number 29 in the court binder is a map of Knin. It, in fact, does indicate the location of the northern barracks. There is a scale on that map which I believe would encompass --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in evidence, but let's -- map 29. I'll give you an answer whether there is any variation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could tell you -- we left where this came from on the lower right-hand corner, it's a Google map search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's frankly where we took it from and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, I'm not criticising that you take it from there but I'm saying that if we have no scale, that we can't verify any measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I point at yesterday, that's what I point at again today. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So let's turn our attention to the next map which is 1D13-0004. Excuse me, then it's got to be this one, 0003, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So looking at this particular map, Mr. Munkelien, we have the correct grid reference as well as the 350 metres. So looking at this, you would agree with me that you had the grid reference wrong and certainly the distance from the front gate, the northern gate of the barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: But as you see on the fence marked with the black here, the fence doesn't run regularly around and I didn't talk about the gate, I was talking about the fence. And the area that was hit by the 6 rockets is within 350 to 500 metres from northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you still maintain that that area that you identified in P70 is the area where it was hit?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, close to where it hit, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you can see from this particular map that's well within 350 metres from the northern fence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have this marked, with the Court's permission, this particular map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which map are we now talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We're now talking about 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The new map. Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D82 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, we will offer into evidence D81 and D82.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the same objection with respect to the distances, the accuracy of the distances, I understand the Court's position on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I used my time to verify it on the basis of map 29 and apart from that it could be 20 or 30 or 40 metres but certainly not more, is there any reason to -- have you done that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, personally, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: However, my exception is to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But are we talking about 10 metres or are we talking about 100 or 200 metres difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't believe we're talking about several hundred metres, Your Honour, how in the interest of accuracy, I think it's important that we have this as a matter of evidence, not to be assumed that it is within a certain range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about the precision of weapons, anything between 350 and 500 and the only thing we're talking about now is about whether the area located by the witness is, well, let's say, close to -- within 350 metres which can be easily verified on the basis of map 29 which you are so kind to draw my attention to, and I really do not understand -- again, it could be 10 or 20 metres, but 10 or 20 metres may be very important if you are drafting the scale of a house, but not if you are talking in terms of 350 to 300 -- to 500 metres whether that's 10 metres more or less and then only, and that's the only thing we are doing is the -- considering the accuracy of what the witness said, nothing more, nothing less, then I still do not understand it. I'll discuss it with my colleagues and we'll decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the two of them, I think, because on both of them, these measurements appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, so pending admission, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's just move on for a bit on the analysis that you did, and you would agree, would you not, sir, that within that 300 -- well, within that particular grid, 9678, the northern barracks is a legitimate military target whoever is trying to take it, whatever army is trying to take it; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It's a legitimate --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Legitimate, I understand.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: -- legitimate target, but that doesn't necessarily give you the permission to fire either artillery or rocket artillery into area that's built up like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And of course that depends when in fact it was fired in as well, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk a little bit about the actual shells that were fired in there. If I could bring up 1D13-0001. Now, before we talk about this particular photograph, Mr. Munkelien, did you take any photographs of the area on the 17th of August?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did anybody?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, who were you with besides Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't recall anybody else than me and Anttila on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you don't recall if anybody took photographs?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't take any photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody in this particular photograph that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that I at least know the British officer to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who is to the left?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this was provided by Mr. Anttila and he maintains this is one of the shells, is it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It can be, yes, I suppose if he said it, it is one of the shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'll offer into evidence what I think would be now D83.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, is the numbering ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D83 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D83 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a British officer to the right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just asking you.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall his name?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the gentleman to the left?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't -- I see -- I've seen the face before but I can't give you the name or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand it's been a long time. You note in your statement P60 that when you took this, and I'm referring to the voluntary statement, Your Honours, you took this shell out of the ground. Was it in soft terrain or where was it that you took it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: It was in the area and I suppose between the house, it was some soft terrain as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you say in your statement that you could determine definitely the calibre of the weapon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the calibre of the weapon is determined by measuring the diameter of the base of the shell, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And based on that, you came to the conclusion that this was an M-63 128-millimetre MRL -- 128-millimetre MRL multi-barrel rocket launcher; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you took this out, and we want to refer back to what we referred to before as your manual, you went back to the headquarters and you went to the manual that you had, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Well, of course we always looked into the manual as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we bring up 1D13-0097 to 0098. This is a two-page document, Your Honour. I think we can just put one number on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D84 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if you could just look at this cover and then if we could go to the next page. Is there any way we can -- can you blow that up a bit? Now, does that appear to be the book and also the photograph that was the UN manual that was issued that describes the M-63 multiple-rocket launcher with the 32 barrels?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, this could be the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This could be the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we'll offer into evidence D84.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D84 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Munkelien, did you do any additional research on the particular shell that you had in order to make the determination that it was from an M-63 128 other than looking at this book?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't recall, but I suppose if you saw on the last photo that went into evidence, you could measure at the bottom of that one and see, yes, it was definitely a rocket like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And you could measure the end of it to come up with the calibre, the 128; right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you did that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: I can't recall I did it with a ruler or something like that, but I suppose we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you said in your statement you would -- it was definitely the calibre --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- so you are sure it was a 128?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk a little bit about 128s. In your training and prior to getting there, did you have instruction as to how many 128s, 128-millimetre multi-barrel rocket launchers were available in the area? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that we were given any figures saying that side had that and the other side had so many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it's important to know when you're looking at a weapons system what side had what weapon as opposed to the other side, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Because that allows you to determine who fired or who possibly fired this particular rocket?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us go to, if we can -- now, if we can just go back to the photograph of D63 for a moment -- excuse me, D83, I apologise. If we can spin that and blow it up a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this particular shell, Mr. Munkelien, if you see the bottom part of it, it's got little long lines throughout. That's where the stabilisation wings were for this weapons system, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And they are important when you fire a 128, you have the wings on there when it's spinning and it stabilises and it goes in the right direction; right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to 1D13-0107. If I could have this marked, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I seek one clarification of one answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier said when Mr. Kehoe asked you about stabiliser fins, you said, "I suppose so," that they were where the lines were. What do you know about it and what is just your supposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never seen the rocket in the firing position, I only seen it after it landed. So I can't tell if they have any wings, I just took it for granted that what the defender said, that was the wings or rest of the wings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I insist that you do not take anything for granted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't understand a question, would you please tell us what you know, what you observed, what you heard, and not take for granted what counsel from whatever party tells you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we can turn to this particular document, if we can have this marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D85 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, just sourcing this, Your Honour, this is a weapons systems chart from a JNA manual setting forth the M-63 128 32-barrel. The lower right-hand corner is from a Croatian Army weapons system with the 12 barrel which is also a 128 but it's known as the MLR rack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now looking at this particular weapon system and on the left-hand side, this is the piece of artillery that went with the weapons system that you looked at from the UN manual, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we look at this particular shell, this is a -- the propulsion system at the bottom of this shell is at the bottom, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: What did you say now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The propulsion system and the stabilization --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you said, your question was: The propulsion system at the bottom of this shell is at the bottom, isn't it," which is a question which, especially if a witness now then takes matters for granted is not a very --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I agree Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the propulsion and the stabilization system in this shell is at the bottom, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this particular shell has no wings, no stabilization wings, does it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, I don't see any wings so I suppose it doesn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that unlike the photograph you viewed, this M-63 does not have stabilization wings?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: No, it does not have any stabilisation wings according to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the bottom that was in this photograph shows a 32-barrel multiple-rocket launcher, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this entire system, this 32-barrel M-63 128 was a system that was in the JNA, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: That was in the Yugoslavian army, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the Army of Republika Srpska had that weapons system as well, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN
utterances.text: The both parties had it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, at the time that -- in August of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to clarify that, both parties had that, we have heard reference to the JNA, we have heard reference to the Republika Srpska army and the parties to the conflict apparently we are talking about is the Croatian army and the Serb RSK army, so if you are talking about both where the JNA was mentioned one second before that, I would like to know, you're referring to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think just to correct the record, Judge, it says HVO. The HVO was the Bosnian-Croat army, the HV is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree. Let's say the Croatian army, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said HV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I misunderstood you and then it's also not reflected correctly on the record. Please proceed. We are talking about the Hrvatska Vojska, if I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, so both the Croatian army and the army of the Republika Srpska had a 128-millimetre weapons system?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But one was the M-128 and the other, for the Croatian army, was the MLR rack 128, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I didn't know that but I thought that both parties had the M-63 128 and maybe they both sides had the rack system as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. But when you use the 128 as we see in this photograph, it doesn't reflect the wings on it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'll offer D85 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to seek some clarification. It appears from the transcript Mr. Kehoe's explanation of the source of the document at page 24, lines 4 through 8 -- I'm sorry, 74, lines 4 through 8, he indicates that this is a weapons system chart from a JNA manual setting forth the M-63 128-32 barrel, the lower right-hand corner is from a Croatian army weapons system with the 12-barrel which is about -- which is also a 128 but it's known as the MLR rack. I just want to be clear whether or not is this a document which was created half from a JNA manual and the picture taken from a Croatian army manual. I'm not clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is correct, Judge, and I've sourced it underneath as exactly where it came from. If you see the writing underneath the legend on the right-hand side, this was from a JNA manual, this particular description of the 128 weapons system where the 128 photograph is from a private collection from the Croatian army. Suffice it to say that the 128 on both the rack and the M-63 is the same exact shell without any wings to it. It's the same shell. The Croatian army was firing at a 12-barrel, the RSK was firing the old JNA in a 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least, I take it you're not giving evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the evidence which you are indicating that you will soon offer evidence, that's well understood. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then what is D85 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could move ahead and turn our attention to 1D13-0108. Your Honour, if I could have this marked for identification at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D86 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Munkelien, in addition to the M-63 128, the army of the Republika Srpska also had an M-77 Oganj system which also fired 128 millimetre, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, according to this sketch ahead of me, this is the RSK rocket system, multi-launcher rocket system,

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, based on your briefing at the time, you were aware that they had this M-77 system, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I was not aware that they had the M-77 system as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there any discussion about the particular -- the other systems that the army of the Republika Srpska had?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, we -- I can't remember that we did any particular discussion on this one or that one, but when we did the crater analysis, we landed on this in my -- M-63, not M-77.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I was -- I've been reminded by my colleague that I said the Republika Srpska and I meant the Republika Srpska Krajina --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- and I just ask that question for the record again. Were you aware that the Republika Srpska Krajina had the M-77 128?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the M-77 128 is a different weapons system than the M-63 128, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: It's a longer flying or had -- it has a definitely longer range. It's the same calibre, 128 millimetre, but the range is 21 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the actual way that it is fired is different in the sense that the M-77 has wings on it where the M-63 is stabilised by the propulsion at the bottom of the shell; correct?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's us turn our attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're talking about stabilisers, do you have specific knowledge on this or are you -- do you know about stabilisers with this specific weapons system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have the MLRS in Norway as well so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- why you are certain about these stabiliser --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- fins or wings. Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we would like to offer into evidence D86.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D86 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn our attention to 1D13-0099.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do apologise, sorry. Can we have this photograph marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D87 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, do you see those photographs, Mr. Munkelien?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And these are photographs of the entire shell of an M-63 in the foreground and an M-77 in the rear; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the M-77, if we can look at it, has stabilisation wings as you mentioned before towards the bottom of the shell, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we'll offer D87 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then just for my understanding, in the large number of projectiles I see, you were referring to the ones --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the foreground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- horizontal in the foreground, the very short one being the M-63, if I well understand, and then the long one being the M-77.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we understood it. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we could just go back to looking at this photograph with the wings, if we could go back to D83. Now, that shell in this individual's hand, we mention has the wing places on there here broken off; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That scars on the bottom can be from the wings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And so if, in fact, these are wings on this particular weapon, then you know now that the M-63 128 was not the weapon system that was fired on Knin either the 4th or the 5th of August, 1995. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Could I have that once again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me take it one step at a time. You agree with me that the M-63 128 millimetre does not have any wings, stabilizing wings on it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that the M-77 128 does have stabilizing wings on it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: It does, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if the shell that is in this photograph has stabilizing wings on it, then you would agree with me that the shell that you picked up on the 17th of August, 1995, was not an M-63 128, was it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: But I don't think I said that this particular grenade that you see in the hand of this English gentleman was the one that we picked up on 17th of August, did I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, would you take issue with the fact that Mr. Anttila has informed the Office of the Prosecutor that it is?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: So that is the photo of the same rocket that we picked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is what Mr. Anttila has informed the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's -- this witness tells us at this moment, Mr. Kehoe, that he cannot identify this projectile as the one he saw at that moment, and if someone else can, then of course I think it has been put to him now several times that others of which the knowledge is still to be established, the basis of their knowledge is still to be established, because I do understand that it's in the hands of an English officer at this moment, it's still not clear to the Chamber at least at this moment how to understand all this, but this witness has now clearly said that on the assumption that this is the shell, that there might be a problem but he is not aware of this shell in the hands on this photograph is the same as the shell he has seen on that particular date. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And just going back and searching your memory, do you recall if the shell that you took or that you seized and measured on the 17th of August of 1995, did it in fact have wings down towards the barrel or places where those wings were broken off?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I can't remember if it had wings or if the wings were broken off but as I state here, we said it was an M-63 MLR, not the rocket, but the M-63 128 MLR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, you would agree with me that if in fact it had wings, that you were incorrect; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point. This question has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the crux of the question. He is now saying that he doesn't recall exactly what it is and the sum and substance of it is if this weapons system has wings on the shell then it's not an M-63 128.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just reread it. Yes, Mr. Kehoe is actually asking whether you are certain about whether the projectile you found had wings or had no wings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not certain if it had wings or no wings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And that particular fact is important to determine what type of shell this is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, that's apparent from the evidence which you presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there's no reason to -- of course it's -- you could even think about other matters such as the length of the projectile, as you see it here, that's even far easier than the wings, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will go into that right now, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And taking that particular issue, you do know, sir, that when you look at the remains of a shell, generally when you get the remains, you get approximately one-third of the original shell given -- one-third third of the original shell after impact, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, looking at this -- well, let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please speak into the microphone, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know who the pre-impact length of an M-63 128 is?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: You mean how far it goes into the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. What I want to ask you the length of a 128. Because what we're getting at is what's remaining, okay? Assuming that we have, as you just said, we have one-third left after impact, do you know, starting from the beginning, what the length of a M-63 128 shell is pre-impact?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I could guess one metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, based on your training, if I said to you 81.4 centimetres, is that about right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And so the post-impact would be approximately 26 centimetres, wouldn't it, if you go by the one-third figure?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: It would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at the 128, the long M-77 128 which you identified.

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you know what the length of that is, that long weapon that we talked about, the M-77?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Close to one and a half to two metres, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if I said to you that it was approximately 260 centimetres, would you think that's about right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So then the post-impact length of that would be about 85 to -- about 85 centimetres; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, look at this photograph. Based on your training and being in the armed forces for the period of time you were, can you give us an approximate length of this particular shell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I think it's perfectly clear that you made your point and we -- of course we could continue to find out that 82.4 divided by 3 is this and then ask the witness to give an estimate of this length all based on the assumption that it is also, in this case, you find one-third of the length and then to find out what we actually mean by one-third is that the part of which is not split, which is still more or less intact or -- but it appears clearly from this picture that if you look at how it bends, that this is a considerable length and without going to all kind of details on which we start guessing and assuming, et cetera, et cetera, that your point has been taken, unless you come up with some concrete evidence, that is, that it has been retrieved, it has been measured, that -- but of course it is -- I take it as you present this in support of the Defence position that if this would be that shell, that then for two reasons, there is a likelihood that it would not be the short -- the short one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that point has been made. But of course there are still a lot of assumptions there on the base of it. I don't know whether it's of great use to explore this further with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Munkelien, that the Croatian Army did not have an M-77 Oganj rocket system?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you took these measurements -- I don't know, Judge, how long you want me to go. I'm about to take Your Honour's hint and move into another area. I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm saying that final conclusions on the basis of a photograph where it's not sure that this is the same, but I do not know whether you come with any evidence at a later stage that this was -- that there is a chain of custody such that we can assume that this is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, as an officer of the Court, what I can tell you is that I take this from the statement by Kari Anttila that this is the shell that Mr. Munkelien and Mr. Anttila retrieved on the 17th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that challenged, Mr. Russo? Let's be very practical.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not challenged so whether true or not, but the -- you do not challenge that Mr. Anttila has told you that what we see on this photograph is the projectile which was found when a crater analysis was made on the 17th of August on which Mr. Anttila and Mr. Munkelien reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is, I believe, what is contained within Mr. Anttila's supplemental witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do understand. But -- well, of course, he will come and testify. But for the time being, being very practical, because to what extent we have to explore this in further detail, of course depends on what the position of the Prosecution in this respect is and the position is that this is a -- that this is what Mr. Anttila has told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore, most likely, you are expecting to confirm that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. So we have that settled. You have made your point that, as it looks here, and comparing the size of ordinary persons with what we see, the bended metal that there is a great likelihood that this comes from a long rather than from a short projectile and it has not at this moment been established which party had what kind of weapons systems. You are very suggestive in that respect but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not done with that yet, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We may hear evidence on that at a later stage or not. Okay. That's where we stand at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to go into another area. Do you want to take a break now or just continue on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A break now will be a good idea. We have a break until 10 minutes to 1.00. Could you give us any indication as to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think I will take the balance of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe that I will take the balance of the session, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then could I ask the other parties ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would estimate one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One and a half hours. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, depending on what happens before me, anywhere between 45 minutes to an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could just say, Judge, I seriously doubt that I will finish within this afternoon on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we already give Mr. Munkelien his break. Could you please escort Mr. Munkelien out of the courtroom. We will resume in approximately 20 minutes, Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I urge the parties to be as efficient as possible in examination in chief and cross-examination. For example, Mr. Kehoe, the issue that this witness mainly served in medical positions, it would have taken me approximately 40 to 50, perhaps 60 seconds to find that out rather than to go through this whole matter in five, six or seven minutes. We have similar matters. You're seeking the witness to repeat matters that are clearly in his statement, to have him repeat that again even where I wonder whether you could ever even expect give another answer, if there are any good reasons to believe that he might be mistaken there. Similarly when we are talking about what a leading question is, if Mr. Russo would not have asked the witness whether a crater analysis is not the same as measuring a distance from an impact to another place, I would not have thought -- it would not even have come to my mind that it would be the same. So therefore, to say they are leading is inadmissible or at least you objected to that leading, I though would not have any impact on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My objection on that score, Judge, was it was generally a pattern of leading. I let it go for a while until we start getting into that, that then becomes the practice and that's when I objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then understood. Then take the strongest example next time to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and not a weak one. Let's -- I urge, therefore, the parties to be as concise in their examination in chief and cross-examination. So Mr. Kehoe, you are encouraged --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to see -- I think you are -- you are convinced that you can do it. So then we will see how you manage to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, we'll resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Russo, no further news about distances on maps? It surprised the Chamber, having checked this for the limited number of metres that this would -- an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to be clear about that. What my objection was is not to whether or not this is actually within 350 metres. What I'm trying to avoid is the situation where we have one piece of evidence which comes in which purports to be by a certain scale and then we have other evidence which comes in with a scale on a similar map or on the same map and then we get into a battle of scales.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't worry about that. Don't worry about that. No scale will escape my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. The objection stands or doesn't stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It no longer stands, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was D81 and D82 if I am correct, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to -- Mr. Munkelien, going back to P60. In P60, your voluntary statement, if we could put that back up on the screen very quickly. The actual -- I guess it's the third page. That's it. In this statement, you say the shells had been fired from the direction of approximately 20 degrees north by north-east. Now, you did a crater analysis, did you not, or looked at where the impact was and then made an analysis as to what direction it came from. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let me show you 1D13-0101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D88 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, I will tell you that this particular map, if we could just -- can we just blow it up a little -- no, it's okay, it's fine. I'm not sure you can get it, it will get outside the margins. This particular map is from the area where you said the impact was, so the grid reference there is WJ9678. Now, from that grid reference on the point of impact, you said that it was approximately 20 degrees north by north-east. And from this map, sir, you would agree with me that that goes up into the area of Strmica, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now Strmica, well, you don't know whether or not this shell was fired on the 4th of August or the 5th of August, do you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you do know that on the 5th of August that the RSK forces were in control of Strmica, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you do know that there was no -- virtually no Serb civilian population in Knin on the 5th because they left or were in the UN camp; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. But this is an accurate assessment of the direction that the weapon was fired from; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn your attention --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'll offer it into evidence, D88. I'm not sure if there was an objection or I'll proffer it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: There was no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D88 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I bring up a sitrep for 5 August 1995, that would be 1D10-0367 to 1D10-0376. Your Honour, this is a sitrep from -- an UNCRO sitrep from 5 August, 1995, if we can just mark it and I will move it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D89 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can turn to page -- it's like four pages in, Shaun, it's 1D10-0370, I don't know if that's easier than taking three pages or ... If we can go to the third paragraph at about 051500 hours, if we could blow that up. No, up, up. I'm sorry. Yes, that one. Actually, that's great.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, Mr. Munkelien, can you read that, it says at about 05 -- "on the 5th of August, at 1500 hours, Arsk soldiers of unknown strength were seen occupying defensive positions in general area of Strmica," and the grid reference is XJ 0091. "Tanks and mortars were seen in the same positions. At 051815, they fired 12 rounds of artillery from Strmica towards Knin." Now, when you were doing your analysis, were you aware of this fact from a UN sitrep report?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I haven't seen this report before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Because you weren't there and --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- and you didn't go back and read it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. When you were doing this crater analysis, do you know where these 12 rounds of artillery that the RSK soldiers fired from the Strmica area into Knin, do you know where they landed?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But Strmica is the direction that the shells came from that you picked out of the ground?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, on 20 degrees, that means north north-east so according to the map that you showed us ahead of this one, it should be from Strmica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on all of the analysis that you've done, Mr. Munkelien, you don't know who fired that --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- weapon system --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when this information was presented, it was I think you told us previously, provided to Colonel Hjertnes?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah. As I said, we reported to the headquarter as such, not to the Colonel but to the headquarter. On special occasion when he had given the specific order, it went directly back to him and reported to the person and not to the headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this particular item was then, if we could pull up -- well, in the provisional assessment, the provisional assessment basically - and I don't want to quote it exactly - said there was concentrated fire on military targets. That's what the provisional assessment said; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the information that you provided in -- to the -- up the line to Colonel Hjertnes and others was then incorporated into that report that was then sent up to the UN, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean we reported and they, like you saw on the reports, was taken away some minor things and then this special issue was reported upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then it was -- were you aware of -- well let me go to 1D10-0239 to 1D10-0248. This is a report of the Secretary-General submitted pursuant to the Security Council Resolution 1009 dated 23 August 1995. Your Honour, can we have this marked and we move it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D90, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And going back to the previous one, I can it was D81 and D82, where the distance -- where you objected initially, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, I did withdraw that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D81 and D82 are admitted into evidence as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going to the second page of this document on paragraph 5. And looking at that first sentence on paragraph 5, it notes that: "On 4 August 1995, the Croatian Army launched the attack in Sectors North and South and Knin fell on 5 August, following concentrated shelling." Were you aware of this report, Mr. Munkelien?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, it's the first time I see it here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ever see a report published in the UN through the Secretary-General or anybody else that specifically criticised, just take the Secretary-General, that specifically criticised the Croatian Army for indiscriminate shelling of Knin on 4 and 5 August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Can you get that again, did I ever see any document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Any report going to the Secretary-General, any media -- any report going to the Secretary-General, let's start with that, that stated that the Croatian Army engaged in indiscriminate fire on the 4th -- indiscriminate artillery fire on the 4th and 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I can't recall any things that I've -- on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you maintain that the provisional assessment was not accurate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's just go back up to the provisional assessment. It might be easier just to look from the document and we're looking at P64. Now, the provisional assessment that's been received into evidence, if we can just pull that up a little -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just push that up a little bit. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it notes that, "In general, shelling was concentrated against military objectives. The damages caused by shelling to civilian establishments is concentrated to the close vicinity of military objectives. Only a few, three to five impacts, is observed in other urban areas." In paragraph 1, it notes that the report is based on a rundown of 70 per cent of Knin town and gives only a brief overview of the situation. Now, it's your position that that assessment is inaccurate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's true, because later, it turned out on the days that it was more shelling or more damage caused by shelling that we found out on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about that. And let us go to paragraph 41 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The statement that I'm referring to is P61. In your statement, sir, you point to several incidents and if you look at your statement paragraph 41, the first statement that you refer to you say that it was inaccurate, said, "On 19 August," and this is midway through paragraph 41. "For example, on 19 August, the patrols concentrating on north-west Knin town have observed 6 houses destroyed by shelling." Now, let's go back to P67 which you use to assess this and let's look at that particular date. On the 19th of August, in P67 in paragraph B where you point to 6 houses destroyed by shelling --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- you were not even on that patrol, were you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: What point are you referring to now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let me take you to this. In your paragraph 31, you say, "The patrols that were conducted after that date indicated that this early assessment was flawed. The UNMO periodical report 27 August confirms that in -- it contains details of shelling damage observed during the patrols. For example, on August 19th, the patrols concentrating on north-west of Knin have observed 6 houses destroyed by shelling." Now, I go back to your document dated the 27th of August which is P67 and I turn to the entry on the 19th of August that mentions 6 houses destroyed by shelling, and it also has the individuals who were on that patrol and you are not one of them, are you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, but it doesn't show here the last one is on the 12th so --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just if you could answer my question. What you highlight in your statement is this entry on the 19th of August where 6 houses are destroyed by shelling and you use that entry to argue that the provisional assessment was inaccurate, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yes, and to my knowledge, either I was on the patrol that was out that day, or I was the man who got the report and reported it back like you see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There are the list of the individuals that are in that patrol under the entry, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, but as you see under C, during the same day, the team also observed the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, there's a -- the patrol names are there and your name isn't there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, that's very correct. But as I also say, there may be a patrol earlier that day that I was part of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that particular patrol that says the 6 houses destroyed --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- there's no grid reference for those particular houses to determine whether or not those houses were in any proximity to military targets, is there?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, there is not. It's only said six north-west of Knin town 94 houses slightly damaged and looted and 6 houses destroyed by shelling and/or burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this information was then given to the chain of command and they made an assessment, excuse me, they made an assessment that the shelling was, for lack of a better term, not indiscriminate and proper; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the characterisation of what was reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will withdraw the question, Judge, and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go down to your next entry. Going back to your statement, your 2008 statement. If you move down to the next entry, "On the next day," and this is again at paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "On the next day, 20 August in the south-west of Knin, 16 houses fully destroyed and another 16 partly destroyed by shelling." If we look again at the entry in P67, do you see the entry in P67, sir?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, for the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Again, sir, your name is not in that patrol.

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: If you could lower it a little bit, I could see the rest of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you could do that, all the way down to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, that's correct, my name is not there, but then I was either on the earlier patrol than this one, or I was the man who was the signaller and got the report directly on radio or in written and made the report to higher headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you remember this specific instance when you were interviewed on the 9th and 10th of January, 2008; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, not only are you not on that patrol, there are no grid references for that location either, are there?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, there is general area. I think that was south-west of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There are no grid references for us to determine whether or not there are military targets in that area?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know, in these particular entries, do you know if there was any fighting going on in those areas?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I don't know since I was not present at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yet did you check, did you check any UN reports or anything to determine before you made this statement in 2008 whether or not there had been fighting taking place in these locations?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You just concluded that the fact that houses had been damaged resulted in your conclusion -- excuse me. Let me withdraw that. You just concluded based on the fact that the houses were damaged that the provisional assessment from Steinar Hjertnes was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw that some of these houses was not added in in the list and that's why we said that was inaccurate when I was there in January 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you say it was not in the list. Isn't it a fact, sir, that another report after the provisional assessment was sent to the UN by Colonel Hjertnes approximately a week later and he told the OTP that the conclusion in that report was consistent with the provisional assessment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo. Are you asking whether it's a fact that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Does he know it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but part of your question was also whether Colonel Hjertnes told the OTP something, and unless there's any reason to assume that this witness would know what Colonel Hjertnes has told the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, he does know some of the things that Colonel Hjertnes told the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but your question was, you say it was not on the list, isn't it a fact, sir, that another report after the provisional assessment was sent to the UN by Colonel Hjertnes approximately one week later and he told the OTP that the conclusions in that report were consistent with the -- provisional assessment. So you're asking this witness without laying any foundation whether he learned what Mr. Hjertnes told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the spirit of precision, Judge, it was a terrible question and I will re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know that Colonel Hjertnes in January of 2008 told the OTP that there was a final assessment, that it was done a week later, and that it was consistent with the provisional assessment? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Were you told at the time that there was is a final assessment done? And I'm talking about back in August of 1995. Were you told at the time that there was a final assessment done?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Other than the document that we see in P60, which is your statement, did you file any -- which is your statement from December of 1995, did you file any other reports indicating specifically that you concluded that the shelling was indiscriminate?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I haven't made any other reports, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us change subjects just a bit, sir, and I want to mention just a few items to you. One of the items that I mention to you is the statement in your 1999 statement -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I have to ask you, you said, and I'm really asking you to keep in full control of the details of your questions as well. You asked the witness, "Other than the document that we see in P60, did you file any other reports indicating specifically that you concluded that the shelling was indiscriminate?" Where do I find in P60 that the witness specifically indicates as a conclusion that the shelling was indiscriminate? I do not read that in P60.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It doesn't say that, but what I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, but therefore just as you are insisting on precision, it's very suggestive and it's the kind of suggestions which we can do without. I mean the points you are making are important enough without --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The -- if I may, Judge. The words indiscriminate aren't used but if you look at the last sentence in that statement, and I did paraphrase this, "Accuracy for this weapon is considered rather poor, 300 to 500 metres, it is an aerial weapon and not designed to be used against specific targets and should not be used in areas where civilian populations can be put in danger."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's still to be established whether this was an area where civilian population was put in danger, whether it was not targeting, as you say, a military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least your suggestion at a distance of 300 or 320 or 330 metres. Let's control our language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we stick to the facts including the text of this report, I think the matters are already important enough and I'm not saying that you're not drawing our attention to important matters but I'm just asking you to be very precise in the language you use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge, and I will be guided by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can direct our attention to 1D13-0089 to 1D13-0091.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D91 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Munkelien, I don't have a hard copy for this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't have but it's okay on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have hard copies if any of the parties ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would -- I don't know how extensive your questioning will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's not very extensive, but it's a lot easier for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you know it's there available for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, with all due respect, Mr. Russo, could you be kind enough to give it to the witness because I think it would just be easier for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It would certainly be faster, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular document is a statement that you gave on 4 September 1999 to the Office of the Prosecutor; is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And carries your signature and initials, initials at the bottom of the pages and your attestation at page 3; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll offer into evidence Exhibit D91.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D91 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, on page 2 of this document, there was a -- and if we can turn to -- yeah, that's the page. If we can turn to that second paragraph, Shaun, please, if we can turn to that 17th of August, in that last sentence of that second paragraph you say "I do not know whether Mr. Anttila completed his assessment of the damages of the buildings in Knin." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila was an engineer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: He was --like I said, I was medical corps, he was in army engineer areas, not necessarily from the engineering corps, not being an engineer himself but being from the engineering corps of the army of Finland.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he have that assignment to assess the damages of buildings in Knin?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: He got that assignment as an UNMO or he could have been picked -- any of the other UNMOs could have been picked for that one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. But you don't know if he completed it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, but now I see that one of the evidences, the thick that one you showed me earlier starting with Sibenek , I know that he was completing the whole Sector South area concerning this damages to buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So these aren't two reports, there's just one?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No. I think it's the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's just shift gears a little bit going into some of the items that you -- were not discussed on direct examination but are in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In your 2008 statement, sir, which is P61, when you are talking about lootings and burnings, at the bottom of that -- the last paragraph -- paragraph 37, that would be P60, or P61, excuse me, P61. If we can just blow up paragraph 37 a little bit. That's what we're going to be talking about. The last couple of sentences in that paragraph, Mr. Munkelien, say, "Because of the ways in which the properties were damaged, I formed the view that there was an element of revenge by the people doing the damage.
