This was also suggested by some of the Serbian civilians that I met." Now, tell me about that, sir, this element of revenge. What kind of damage was in there that people were coming back to exact revenge?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: If you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the form of the question. The question was, "People coming back for revenge." I don't believe that's a correct characterisation of what the witness indicated. He indicated that there was an element of revenge to the destruction in general, I don't see any indication of people coming back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The indication is that the Croats came back into the area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- if -- perhaps it's best to put to the witness exactly the words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. If we can just go to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What did you mean by these two sentences?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I mean that it was definitely looting going on the whole time, and if you start with the rings and the gold, if they had any, and the money that they started to loot in the beginning, then they came back and took the inside furniture, and then, as I say, they ended up with taking the doors and the door frames and the windows. It looks like nobody should ever go back to inhabit this house again from that particular part of the population that had been living there before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you use the word "revenge" when you put that in this statement, were you aware of what happened to the Croatian population from 1991 to 1995 in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I was definitely knowing that I think no sides were without guilt in this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So these people that -- when you use the word "revenge" were you using that word in -- knowing what had happened to the Croats between 1991 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I didn't use it for discriminating or anything like that. I was just using it as a description of what I felt was happening. It was definite that they didn't want people to come back to that house again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in the lootings themselves -- by the way, you note in your statement at paragraph 34 of that same statement that, "As far as identifying soldiers who were looting by their unit, although I can say that I saw Croatian soldiers looting, I saw Croatian soldiers who had the insignia of the 4th Guards Brigade on their arm. I cannot recall that I witnessed members of the 4th Guards Brigade looting." Now, what is the time frame of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I can't just recall, but remember, I was there from the 14th of August until the 1st of December. So during that period, and it -- towards October-November, it diminished in frequency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in August and in September, were you aware of where the 4th Guards Brigade was fighting?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I was not aware where they were fighting. I only saw insignias and uniforms from HV soldiers in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had regular briefings in UN headquarters, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were aware, when you got there, that the fighting between the Croatian Army and the Serbs, be it the Krajina Serbs or the Bosnian Serbs was now [Realtime transcript read in error "not"] taking place up in the Bosnian-Croatian border?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that started -- was going on when you got there on the 14th, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And the regular soldiers of the Croatian army, of course, you knew from the debriefings were up there fighting, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, they were up there fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that fighting continued through almost your entire tour in Sector South, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting Your Honour but I believe the transcript incorrectly, at line 19, page 108 says the fighting was not taking place up in the Bosnian-Croatian border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That apparently is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to this looting issue, if we can go back to D91. Now, in D91 if we can move in the last paragraph, "In particular, I remember ..." It says, "In particular, I remember one incident when I was on patrol to Plavno valley together with one more officer. I do not remember his name. And a female Serbian interpreter in the end of August, beginning of September 1995. Moving along the small road into one of the hamlets, we noticed some military vehicles, trucks and vans, on the road and several HV soldiers entering and exiting the houses. We left our interpreter in the car and came up to the soldiers. They were definitely the Croatian soldiers wearing military uniforms and guns. We explained to them that we were trying to help the people and that they were not supposed to be there and asked them not to make things" it says worth but I believe means worse, "make things worse." It was a very difficult situation. We were not armed. I noticed that there was some electronic equipment in the cars. So those soldiers were definitely in the process of looting. After we spoke to them, they left. We went to speak to local Serbs. There were only three elderly people left. They told us that the looters were coming to the area very often. As I understood on that day, those Serbs were not visited by the looters. The soldiers looted only abandoned houses." Mr. Munkelien, I want to address your attention to this line here, "So after we spoke to them, they left." You had a conversation with these -- in uniform, and told them not to do it and they went away, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They didn't tell you that they had orders to do this, did they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell us that they had orders. It was a private initiative, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So private initiative, these guys were doing it on their own?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, but they were still in uniform, still using military vehicles, still using military weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They never told you that anybody gave them permission to do that, did they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, nevertheless, you said you think it was private initiative. On what was that thought based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think it was an overall order from any parties to do the looting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now that's clear. That's as a matter of fact are the two ends of a long scale, private initiative or an overall order. That's one extremely to the one side and the other one to the other side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was it based or was it just an impression that you saw a couple of people not in any way organised going into the houses and is that on the basis of that impression that you say, "I think it was a private initiative"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but since they gave in so easily when the unarmed UNMOs spoke to them, I think it was something like that that they felt, okay, we are on the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's your conclusion on the basis of their response?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On what you told them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back to some of the documents that were received in evidence during the Prosecution case concerning burnings and damage to houses and I believe what we were talking about was the -- bear with me one moment -- it is P66, if we could bring that up on the screen. Now, this is the document that you said was prepared by Kari Anttila; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And that you noted for us that -- and if we can just shift back to P65, that this is the type of form that was used among other -- was this the only form used to put this document together?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That was one of the forms and in addition, it was the daily sitreps, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sitreps that you did all the time?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In this particular form, in line 1, if we can blow up line 1. It notes that this is the Plavno Valley including Jovici, Basinac, Torbice, Grmusa, Stojakovici and this is by the Podkonje team, right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to this document and we go back -- the document I want to take you back to is 66. Mine says 200 -- it says 207 damaged with these villages there. And on the -- now, if we turn to the one, two, three, four -- on the fifth page, I believe Team Podkonje starts. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I see on this document that we have the villages of Torbice, Grmusa and Stojakovici. Where are the villages of Jovici and Basinac, B-a-s-i-n-a-c? Could you take a look for me please.

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yes, I have been looking and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They're not there?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: They are not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if -- and there are entries for this document in some villages where there is no damage whatsoever; right? Like Grmusa and Torbice right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: At least no figures there, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, there is not even any name for the two villages for Jovici and Basinac, is there?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No. Maybe that was small so it was added into the neighbour's village or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, all of these villages that are here Basinac, Trice and I'm reading through the villages in P65 Grmusa and Stojakovici, they were all little tiny villages, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So they are no bigger or no smaller than Jovici or Basinac?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, and there is nothing on the next page either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you would say at this point that P66 is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that because it's -- according to what they had for information, it's good enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness asked whether there was anything on the next page. Perhaps you answered that question. Of course we can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can go to the next page, I'm sorry. I think he looked at the next page and said there was nothing there either but we can certainly go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought he was asking whether there was anything on the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise. I do apologise. I thought he said if we can turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last -- on the top page is also Plavno valley but according to, as I said, the information he had, he has made a list and if he slipped some, that's okay. It's not on the list so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it's okay. Now, the other matter here was data that was -- the document maintains data on population left in Sector South destroyed houses after Operation Storm. Did you know that, if I may, for instance, on page -- one, two, three -- four, beginning with Donji Lapac. Now, there's a whole listing of Donji Lapac there, right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you are aware that this particular area -- well, that the area in Knin in any event, was in the Split military district under the -- generally in the Split military district, you are aware of that, are you not?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Now you're telling me so now I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So were you aware, for instance, that Donji Lapac was not in the Split military district?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Likewise if you can turn to -- would it be best to give you the page number which is at the bottom, 0054-8199. Should be Otocac. Otocac, that was likewise not -- do you know, that was not in the Split military district?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I didn't -- you tell me, so yes, I said?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir -- so you don't know?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said that this P65 which is the type of form that was used to list some of damages to buildings was used in conjunction with the sitreps; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you know where any of these documents are?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I mean some of the sitreps from the different teams is taken care of, some is not, as far as I read this court earlier because this from Otocac, that was given in to Sector South like Donji Lapac, like Podkonje or Knin Team, they all went in like a normal sitrep with attachments or something like that and that was then the basic for the report that you have as evidence in front of me on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean when you're putting these documents together, obviously it's important to be as accurate as possible, right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we've obviously maintained in P65 at least two villages that were in one of these reports didn't make it to Mr. Anttila's final report; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And by the way, if we look at what the Prosecution has put in, and if I can just get the correct number, P68, which is the summary. In this summary that you put into evidence is a listing of sitreps that detail humanitarian violations from August to September; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the sitreps should, in fact, incorporate as many of them do, the number of houses that are burnt; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, it should mirror the one that given in that report, because then you have the sitreps from the different teams, then you have the sector headquarter, and then the humanitarian part of these reports is taken out on this one because this is humanitarian sitreps. And then you have other things, military transport, movements of troops like everything that we reported in the teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we move back to P66 and go to the last page. Mr. Anttila has concluded that with the number of 21.744 buildings, approximately 18.000 are partially or completely damaged; right?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah, I see the figures. There is a total down there so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right. So my question to you, sir, is: Do you know that the amount of houses that were damaged and destroyed that is set forth in the summary of humanitarian violations, which is P68, amounts to approximately 1.350?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that's a discrepancy of almost 15.000 between the sitreps where this information is going to be contained, and the information that Mr. Anttila put together, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: Yeah. And I suppose this is the right figures because definitely we were the, and I quote, "the eyes and the ears of the Security Council" so if somebody is reliable, we definitely United Nations Military Observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But the information that is set forth in Mr. Anttila's statistics are not set forth in this summary of humanitarian violations, is it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I suppose I don't need to answer that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well the answer is no, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: I think you are putting me into words and I didn't say no, so could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the information that was in this statistical compilation by Mr. Anttila, that information on the number of houses is not contained in the sitreps that you produced into evidence previous today --

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: But the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, that are supposed to list the number of partially destroyed and destroyed houses; isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: RSK
utterances.text: The list that's there is definitely the right figures for houses looted, burned, damaged during this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When the witness was hesitant to answer your question and when he asked you to repeat the question, you came up with a rather different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're aware of that. The second time you refer to sitreps where the first time you refer to something totally different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's all the same document, Judge, it's the same document. The humanitarian summary is the sitreps that were put together in P68. It sitreps and it's called the summary of humanitarian violations but it's the same document that the Prosecution put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first time your question was, "But the indication that is set forth in Mr. Anttila's statistics are not set forth in this summary of humanitarian violations."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the summary then is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is the sitreps. Is what the Prosecution put in that I objected to, which is the sitreps that were taken out and just put into this summary that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well then at least this question is quite confusing and quite differently phrased from what you did later where you specifically referred to the sitreps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In an effort to clarify exactly what I was talking about, Judge, because the document, while it says summary, is, in fact, a summary of sitreps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at the clock. We are already far beyond where we should be. Mr. Munkelien, apart from your testimony, as you are aware of, we would like to see you back tomorrow at 9.00 in the same courtroom. You could perhaps already follow Mr. Usher but not until I have instructed you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether the testimony already given or still to be given. Yes? Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please go out with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, even though we took six minutes extra, you didn't manage. How much time do you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 15, 20 minutes, I can just wrap up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 15, 20 minutes, okay, then I'll keep to you 15 minutes for tomorrow as matters stand now. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I can do between now and tomorrow is I'll speak with Mr. Mikulicic about trying to at least agree that we're not going to cover the same areas and if they are going to cover areas that I may have covered, then we will drop those so we will try and shrink the time that is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Kuzmanovic or Mr. Mikulicic, what -- I've forgotten what your early indication was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had said 45 minutes to an hour. Some of the ground has been covered already, we will speak with Mr. Cayley and we will try to reduce. I will try not to be more than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then try to see whether we can finish cross-examination by 10.00 tomorrow morning. And then we'll see -- Mr. Russo, do you have any idea on how much time you would need in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Very brief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very brief. So then -- if we give it some effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt. You said finished by 10.00 tomorrow. If Mr. Mr. Kehoe takes 15 minutes, is that 45 minutes for the other two Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand that but --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I said originally I would take an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic said half an hour. I said I would try and reduce that but I don't think I can reduce an hour and a half to sort of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. No. Then I misunderstood you. Yes. Let's then -- that will take us beyond the first break then considerably. Then at least the next witness we could expect to start giving testimony somewhere in the second session tomorrow morning and the time scheduled for the next witness was ... are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe it was two hours, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just looking ahead, whether we would sit during all the remaining days in full because I received some information that you might -- that the -- that the Prosecution might run out of witnesses later this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a possibility, depending on the length of the cross-examination of our next witness, that we could have a bit of a gap on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. Mr. Kuzmanovic, anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I was just going to say that I had originally estimated anywhere between 45 minutes to an hour and I think I can be done in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber would like to receive your new estimates then after you have discussed the matters among yourselves tomorrow before the -- before we start.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to make clear that our estimate was two hours for Mr. Dreyer, our next witness, but I don't believe it's actually going to take that long so we are going to have a bit of a -- some more time left over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do the other parties have already any idea on whether the next witness would take relatively long or relatively short in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think I will be a little while with this gentleman. I will be a little while, just because it's a 92 ter statement, he's got three or four statements, four trips on the 4th of August. There could be some detail there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A little while means what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At least a couple of hours, I would say at least. I don't want to say just two hours at this point. Depending on how it goes. The problem with this witness, and I will be very candid with this, I did talk to Mr. Tieger about this, that he makes some very global statements that frankly I've tried to get behind and I have not been able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say a little while, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We, with apologies to the Chamber that follows in this courtroom for our late finish, we'll adjourn and resume tomorrow 9.00 same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th of April, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.58 p.m.
